answer: One workable rule links each new account to the wallet that funded its first bond, and every extra child of the same root must lock double the previous bond for thirty epochs. A tree of n fakes ties up about 2^n units, while an honest user with one or two accounts stays near the cost nadir. Laundering funds through fresh wallets only adds hops, each paying its own fee and bond, like cracking walnut after walnut for one kernel. The rule is plain ledger arithmetic, not a cloudy opal of hidden heuristics, so anyone can audit it.
